```{definition} destructors.body_typing
:lean: Destructors/Typing:BodyTyped Destructors/Typing:DeclarationsTyped Destructors/Typing:ProgramTyped
:uses: destructors.declarations destructors.finished_environment destructors.drop_typing

Check every [declared destructor body](#claim-destructors.declarations) starting with exactly `self: given C`,
where `C` is its declaring class with its whole view. Its statements must type
check and leave a [finished environment](#claim-destructors.finished_environment). Check ordinary functions and methods using their declared parameters and
result types from the [Functions signatures](functions.md#claim-functions.signatures),
requiring a finished environment after evaluation of any return expression.
Check the top-level program from the empty environment with the same final
condition.

All declared destructor signatures are available while checking each body.
A call checks [droppability](#claim-destructors.droppable), not an inline expansion of the called body. The
whole declaration table is accepted only when every declared body checks.
This permits recursive destructor calls, including `drop self`.

The inherited rules for declarations, expressions, fresh bindings, and
unpacking otherwise apply; the [appendix](#claim-destructors.inherited)
identifies those rules. Assignment is not part of this layer.
```

```{definition} destructors.declarations
:lean: Destructors/Syntax:Name Destructors/Syntax:Signature.WellFormed Destructors/Syntax:Declaration Destructors/Syntax:Statement Destructors/Syntax:Statement.dropClass Destructors/Syntax:Body Destructors/Syntax:Program
:uses: shared.declarations shared.struct

A declaration retains [Shared's name, kind, and ordered fields](shared.md#claim-shared.declarations). A `class`
declaration may additionally contain one destructor, written `drop { body }`,
where `body` is a sequence of statements. The destructor has no parameters or
result; its initial local binding is `self`, a [uniquely owned whole instance](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.types)
of the declaring class. A `struct` or `shared struct` has no destructor body
in this layer.

The core distinguishes ordinary function names, qualified method names, and
`drop(C)` destructor names. A destructor is stored as a declaration with exactly
one parameter `→self` of its owning class and no result. Names must be unique;
ordinary methods cannot collide with destructor names.

Classes without destructors remain legal. Their instances must be consumed
through [explicit unpacking](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.bindings), possibly after being moved to another owner.
[Struct fields still have only struct types](shared.md#claim-shared.struct), and classes still cannot be shared.
The inherited declaration restrictions are collected in the
[appendix](#claim-destructors.inherited).
```

```{definition} destructors.drop_typing
:lean: Destructors/Typing:DropTyped Destructors/Typing:StatementTyped
:uses: destructors.droppable shared.typing.giving

The new statement is `drop p`, where `p` is a [place](shared.md#claim-shared.syntax) (a local followed by zero or
more field names). An [environment](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.environments) `Γ` maps local names to types or empty slots.
Write `Give(Γ, p) = (T, Γ′)` for [Shared's static ordinary-give operation](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.giving),
recalled in the [appendix](#claim-destructors.inherited).

The surface statement elaborates to a struct-discard operation or to
`drop(C)(p→)`, a core call to the [destructor name](#claim-destructors.declarations)
with no destination. The class name comes from the given value's type. This
elaboration inserts no implicit drops and adds no receiver-call sugar.

The rule is:

- Compute `Give(Γ, p) = (T, Γ′)`.
- [Require `Droppable(T)`](#claim-destructors.droppable).
- Check the following statements under `Γ′`.

For a class this moves the value out of its source and calls its destructor.
For a struct, dropping the resulting value invokes no code and destroys no
object. Struct storage is treated as if garbage collected.

For structs, use exactly the ordinary-give effect.
A given struct moves out, leaving an empty slot; a shared struct reference is
copied, leaving its source initialized. The empty local binding is retained,
as for ordinary give. No binding is removed.
```

```{definition} destructors.droppable
:lean: Destructors/Typing:Droppable
:uses: destructors.declarations shared.typing.types shared.struct

The *droppability judgment* `Droppable(T)` says that an explicit drop can consume a value of
type `T`, using a well-formed declaration table. Types retain [Shared's permissions and signed views](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.types), summarized in the
[appendix](#claim-destructors.inherited).

| Type of value | Condition for `Droppable(T)` |
| --- | --- |
| Struct, including shared struct | Any well-formed permission and view allowed for that nominal type. |
| Class | Given permission, a whole declared view, and a [declared destructor](#claim-destructors.declarations). |

“Whole” means that [view normalization](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.normalization) exposes the entire declared value, not
merely every currently visible field. A partially moved class cannot invoke its
destructor. An omitted field is [unknown](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.views), not evidence that the field is empty.
```

```{definition} destructors.finished_environment
:lean: Destructors/Typing:Finished Destructors/Step:StoreFinished
:uses: shared.struct destructors.drop_typing

An environment is *finished* when each binding is either empty or has a [struct
type](shared.md#claim-shared.struct). A class binding is an outstanding obligation even if its class has a
destructor, its view is partial, or all of its fields are empty. A frame may
finish only when its statement sequence is exhausted and its environment is
finished.

A *[frame](functions.md#claim-functions.machine)* owns a local environment and a sequence of statements still to run.
There is one program frame and one fresh frame per active function, method,
or destructor call.
Names are local to their frame; a destructor cannot access its caller's locals.

Moving a class to another local transfers the obligation. Storing it inside a
class transfers the obligation to that owner; [unpacking](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.bindings) transfers obligations
to the resulting field bindings. No class can be hidden inside a struct,
because struct fields must themselves have struct types.

Frame completion discards remaining struct bindings without running code.
It inserts no drops and performs no implicit unpacking.
```

```{definition} destructors.inherited
:lean: Destructors/Syntax:Parameter Destructors/Syntax:Signature Destructors/Typing:ResultTyped Destructors/Typing:DestinationTyped Destructors/Typing:SequenceTyped
:uses: shared.declarations shared.struct shared.syntax shared.state shared.give shared.typing.types shared.typing.giving shared.typing.expressions shared.typing.patterns shared.typing.statements

The preceding rules use the following Shared machinery unchanged, except for
imposing the [completion condition](#claim-destructors.finished_environment) defined above; frames already exist in Shared.
These links identify the full inherited definitions; this summary fixes their
role in this layer.

| Machinery | Inherited meaning |
| --- | --- |
| [Declarations and kinds](shared.md#claim-shared.declarations) | Nominal names and ordered named fields; classes, structs, and shared structs. Only structs satisfy [struct(T)](shared.md#claim-shared.struct); struct fields have struct types. |
| [Syntax](shared.md#claim-shared.syntax) | Places start at locals and follow named fields. Expressions give a place, give-share a place, or construct an object from ordered argument expressions. Bindings use fresh local names. |
| [Storage](shared.md#claim-shared.state) | References carry modes and object identifiers. Object fields contain references or empty slots. Allocation uses fresh, monotonically allocated identifiers. |
| [Types and views](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.types) | Given and shared permissions, whole declared types, and signed views. Positive entries expose whole subtrees, negative entries record empty slots, and omissions are unknown. |
| [Ordinary give](shared.md#claim-shared.give) | Move through a unique path, emptying its final slot; copy through shared access, promoting a unique final reference if necessary. [Static give](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.giving) computes the result type and source environment. |
| [Construction](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.expressions) | Evaluate arguments left to right; require whole declared argument types. Shared structs construct shared references immediately. |
| [Unpacking](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.patterns) | A unique result can be unpacked with `C → { fields }`, removing the container and transferring its field slots to bindings. Every direct field's status must be known; transferred objects may themselves be partial. Shared references cannot be unpacked. |

Shared's completion bound of one step per statement plus initial-frame exit
does not carry over.
Rootedness now counts all live frames; eager GC removes unreachable struct
storage at each transition boundary. Class obligations survive until explicit consumption.
```

```{definition} functions.calls
:lean: Functions/Syntax:Statement Functions/Syntax:Body Functions/Syntax:Declaration Functions/Syntax:Program
:uses: functions.signatures shared.syntax shared.typing.patterns

A *[value expression](shared.md#claim-shared.syntax)* \\(e\\) and *[binding pattern](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.patterns)* \\(b\\) are inherited from
Shared (see the [appendix](#claim-functions.inherited)). An *optional call
destination* \\(d\\) is either a fresh local name or absent. The core syntax is:

\\[
\begin{aligned}
d &::= \mathsf{none}\mid x, \\
t &::= \mathsf{let}\ b=e \mid d\mathrel{:=}\mathsf{call}\ a({\overline e}), \\
r &::= \mathsf{none}\mid e, \\
B &::= ({\overline t};\ \mathsf{return}\ r), \\
D &::= (\sigma,B).
\end{aligned}
\\]

Here \\(t\\) is a statement, \\(r\\) an optional return expression, \\(B\\) a
body, and \\(D\\) a declaration pairing a [signature](#claim-functions.signatures) with its body. The call notation above is metasyntax:
`let x = f(args);` supplies destination `x`, while `f(args);` supplies none.
A method call is `C.method(receiver, args)`, with its receiver as argument zero.
There is no receiver-based call sugar.

A body stores its final return separately from its statement list. `return;`
and falling off the end both mean no return expression. There are no early
returns. Receivers, arguments, and returned values use call-free expressions;
write nested calls as successive statements.

A program contains a [nominal class table](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.declarations) \\(\Delta\\), a declaration table
\\(F\\) listing callable-name/declaration pairs, and a top-level statement
list. Method lookup uses the qualified name, not runtime dispatch. There is
no overloading. These are abstract syntax definitions, not a source parser.
```

```{definition} functions.inherited
:lean: Shared/Syntax:Value Shared/State:State Shared/Step:Give Shared/Step:Eval Shared/Step:EvalArgs Shared/Unpacking:Pattern Shared/Unpacking:Bind Shared/Typing:ExprTyped Shared/Typing:ArgsTyped
:uses: shared.declarations shared.struct shared.state shared.give shared.typing.types shared.typing.expressions shared.typing.patterns

The call machine and its typing judgments live in `Functions/`. They explicitly
use Shared's call-free expressions, storage, and binding judgments. There is
no change to those definitions in this layer:

| Machinery | Inherited behavior |
| --- | --- |
| [Nominal kinds](shared.md#claim-shared.declarations) | Classes cannot be shared; struct fields have struct types. |
| [Storage](shared.md#claim-shared.state) | References carry modes; slots hold a reference or are empty; allocation is monotonic. |
| [Views](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.types) | Positive entries expose whole subtrees, negative entries record empty slots, and omissions are unknown. |
| [Giving](shared.md#claim-shared.give) | Unique access moves; shared access copies, promoting a unique final stored reference when necessary. |
| [Expressions](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.expressions) | Constructor arguments are evaluated left to right and require whole declared types. Shared structs construct shared references immediately. |
| [Unpacking](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.patterns) | Unpacking requires unique access and known status for every direct field, removes the container, and transfers its field slots to fresh bindings. |

The call syntax, frame stores, and call/return judgments are defined separately
in Functions. Assignments, destructors, branches, loops, and borrowing remain
outside this layer.
```

```{definition} functions.machine
:lean: Functions/Step:Store Functions/Step:Frame Functions/Step:Configuration Functions/Step:Configuration.running Functions/Step:Configuration.initial
:uses: functions.calls shared.state

Each call has a *frame* \\(\phi\\) containing its local store \\(V\\), [remaining
body](#claim-functions.calls) \\(B\\), and destination \\(d\\) for its result in the caller. A store maps
local names to references or empty slots. The frame stack \\(K\\) lists the
active frame first, followed by suspended callers. The heap \\(H\\) and next
object identifier \\(n\\) belong to the whole machine:

\\[
\phi=(V,B,d),\qquad K=[\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_j],\qquad
M=\langle H,n,K\rangle.
\\]

Only the active frame's locals are accessible to expressions. For evaluation,
combine them with the heap and counter to form [Shared's state](shared.md#claim-shared.state) \\(S=(H,V,n)\\).
The Lean helper `Configuration.running` constructs a configuration from such a
state, an active body, a caller stack, and a result destination.

The initial configuration has an empty heap, counter zero, and **one frame**:
empty locals, the program's statements, no return expression, and no destination.
```

```{definition} functions.signatures
:lean: Functions/Syntax:Name Functions/Syntax:Parameter Functions/Syntax:Signature Functions/Syntax:receiver Functions/Syntax:Signature.WellFormed
:uses: shared.typing.types shared.struct

A *callable name* \\(a\\) identifies either a global function \\(f\\) or a method
named \\(m\\) of nominal type \\(C\\). Parameter names \\(x\\) are local variables. A
*signature type* \\(T\\) is a [whole nominal type](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.types) with an explicit permission
\\(Q\\); it carries no partial view.

\\[
\begin{aligned}
a &::= f \mid C.m, & Q &::= {\to} \mid \mathsf{shared}, \\
T &::= Q\ C, & P &::= x:T, \\
R &::= \mathsf{none} \mid T, & \sigma &::= ({\overline P})\;R.
\end{aligned}
\\]

Here \\(P\\) is a parameter, \\(R\\) an optional result type, and
\\(\sigma\\) a signature.

`shared[]` abbreviates the same permission as `shared`. The model calls `→`
permission `given`. A result annotation follows the parameter list directly;
its absence denotes no result. There is no implicit parameter permission.

A method's first parameter is written `→self` or `shared self`. These elaborate
to the parameter named `self` with type `→ C` or `shared C`, respectively,
where `C` is the enclosing nominal type. No `self: Type` surface form is
provided. Ordinary function parameters cannot be named `self`.

A well-formed signature has distinct parameter names and [admissible parameter
and result types](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.well_formed_types). A method must have its correctly named and typed receiver
first. In particular, classes admit only given access, shared structs admit
only shared access, and ordinary structs admit either.
```

```{definition} given.classes
:lean: Unique/Syntax:ClassName Unique/Syntax:FieldName Unique/Syntax:Class

This language studies transfer of ownership. Variables and object fields hold
references to objects. Giving a reference moves it to its destination and leaves
its source empty; constructing an object moves references into its fields.

A *class declaration* \\(d\\) names a class and its fields. Write \\(C\\) for
a class name in \\(\mathsf{ClassName}\\), and \\(f\\) for a field name in
\\(\mathsf{FieldName}\\). The field count \\(n\\) is a natural number,
including zero:

\\[
d ::= \mathsf{class}\ C\ \{f_1,\ldots,f_n\}.
\\]

Fields are distinct and listed in constructor-argument order. They have names
but no declared types.
An empty class still has objects, so this language needs no primitive values.
Subscripts and primes distinguish names in the same category.
```

```{definition} given.collections
:lean: Common/FiniteMap:FiniteMap

Write \\(A\rightharpoonup B\\) for *finite partial maps* from domain \\(A\\)
to codomain \\(B\\), and \\(\mathsf{List}(A)\\) for finite ordered sequences
of elements of \\(A\\).
```

```{definition} given.evaluation
:lean: Unique/Step:Eval Unique/Step:EvalArgs Unique/Step:State.allocate
:uses: given.classes given.syntax given.programs given.state given.storage_places given.resolution given.identities given.update given.slots

*Expression evaluation*, written

\\[
\Delta\vdash\langle S,e\rangle\Downarrow\langle S',\alpha\rangle,
\\]

produces an [owning reference](#claim-given.slots) \\(\alpha\\) and updated [storage](#claim-given.state) \\(S'\\).
The following rules define successful evaluation, including nested expressions.

**Give.** [Resolve the place](#claim-given.resolution) and [empty its slot](#claim-given.update). Return the reference taken:

\\[
\frac{\href{#claim-given.resolution}{S\vdash p\Downarrow q:\alpha}}{
  \Delta\vdash\langle S,p\mathord{\to}\rangle
  \Downarrow\langle \href{#claim-given.update}{S[q\leftarrow\bot]},\alpha\rangle
}
\quad\text{Give}
\\]

**Construct.** Evaluate the arguments from left to right, then allocate the
object and put their results into its fields in declaration order.

\\[
\frac{
  \begin{gathered}
    \href{#claim-given.programs}{\Delta(C)}=[f_1,\ldots,f_n] \\
    \Delta\vdash\langle S_{i-1},e_i\rangle
      \Downarrow\langle S_i,\alpha_i\rangle
      \quad\text{for each }i=1,\ldots,n \\
    \beta\notin\operatorname{dom}(O_n)
  \end{gathered}
}{
  \Delta\vdash\langle S_0,\mathsf{new}\ C(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\rangle
    \Downarrow\langle S',\beta\rangle
}
\quad\text{Construct}
\\]

where \\(S_0\\) is the starting storage and \\(S_i\\) is the storage after
the first \\(i\\) arguments, with

\\[
\begin{aligned}
S_n &= \langle O_n,V_n,\nu_n\rangle, \\
\beta &= \href{#claim-given.identities}{\mathsf{obj}(\nu_n)}, \\
O' &= O_n[\beta\mapsto C\{f_1:\alpha_1,\ldots,f_n:\alpha_n\}], \\
S' &= \langle O',V_n,\nu_n+1\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\\]

Here \\(\operatorname{dom}(O_n)\\) is the set of allocated identities, and
\\(O_n[\beta\mapsto o]\\) adds the fresh object's entry.

With no arguments, there are no argument premises and allocation uses
\\(S_n=S_0\\). Argument results remain owned by the ongoing evaluation until
placed in the new object's fields; they are not copied.

An empty slot, a missing field, or an unknown class has no successful evaluation.
Giving the same slot twice as constructor arguments fails on the second give.
An expression runs within one statement transition, but it can still fail.
```

```{definition} given.gc
:lean: Unique/State:Live Unique/Frames:State.collect Unique/Frames:Configuration.collect
:uses: given.machine given.state

*Reachability* starts at an initialized slot of the [live frame](#claim-given.machine) and follows
[initialized object fields](#claim-given.slots). Write \\(\mathsf{Live}_S(\alpha)\\) when this reaches
object \\(\alpha\\). An absent frame has no roots.

*Eager collection* retains exactly reachable object entries. For object data
\\(D\\) (its class tag and field slots), define:

\\[
\operatorname{gc}(K)=\langle
 [(\alpha,D)\in O\mid\mathsf{Live}_{S_K}(\alpha)],\nu,F\rangle.
\\]

Here \\(S_K\\) uses the frame's locals, or an empty variable store if the
frame is absent. Collection preserves surviving objects and their identifiers,
the allocation counter, and the frame. It invokes no user code. With no frame,
it removes the entire heap.

The Lean definition is a mathematical reachability filter, not an executable
traversal. Collection runs after whole statements and frame exit, never between
constructor operands or while an expression result awaits binding.
```

```{definition} given.identities
:lean: Unique/Syntax:ObjectId
:uses: given.programs

An *object identity* \\(\alpha\\) is a tagged natural number. The tag keeps
identities distinct from ordinary numbers. We also use \\(\beta\\) for an
object identity; \\(\operatorname{index}\\) extracts its number:

\\[
\alpha,\beta\in\mathsf{ObjectId}
  =\{\mathsf{obj}(n)\mid n\in\mathbb N\},
\qquad
\operatorname{index}(\mathsf{obj}(n))=n.
\\]
```

```{definition} given.lookup
:lean: Unique/State:Stored
:uses: given.state given.storage_places given.slots

For \\(S=\langle O,V,\nu\rangle\\), write \\(S[q]=s\\) for *slot lookup* at a
[storage place](#claim-given.storage_places).
It is a partial operation, defined by:

\\[
\begin{aligned}
S[x] &= V(x) &&\text{when }V(x)\text{ is defined}, \\
S[\alpha.f_i] &= s_i
  &&\text{when }O(\alpha)=C\{f_1:s_1,\ldots,f_n:s_n\},\ 1\leq i\leq n.
\end{aligned}
\\]

Lookup has no result for an absent variable, object, or field. An existing empty
slot has the defined result \\(\bot\\). An occupied slot contains an object
identity, not that object's data; the data is in \\(O\\).
```

```{definition} given.machine
:lean: Unique/Frames:Frame Unique/Frames:Configuration Unique/Frames:Configuration.running Unique/Frames:Configuration.initial Unique/Frames:Configuration.state
:uses: given.state given.syntax

A *frame* \\(f=(V,P)\\) owns its local variable store \\(V\\) and remaining
[statements](#claim-given.syntax) \\(P\\). The [program](#claim-given.programs) has one initial frame; after its exit there is
no frame. Heap objects \\(O\\) and the allocation counter \\(\nu\\) live outside it:

\\[
K=\langle O,\nu,F\rangle,\qquad F::=\mathsf{none}\mid\mathsf{some}(V,P).
\\]

For expression evaluation, combine the live frame's locals with the heap and
counter as the [storage](#claim-given.state) \\(S=\langle O,V,\nu\rangle\\). Write
\\(\operatorname{run}(S,P)=\langle O,\nu,\mathsf{some}(V,P)\rangle\\).
The pair \\(\langle S,P\rangle\\) used by local statement rules is an
observation of that live frame, not a terminal program state.

Initially \\(K=\operatorname{run}(S_{\emptyset},P)\\), including when \\(P=[]\\).
Exhausting the statements leaves a live frame whose bindings can still be
inspected. A separate exit step pops it. There are no nested scopes or calls in
this layer; Functions will extend this single-frame lifetime to a stack.
```

```{definition} given.patterns
:lean: Unique/Unpacking:Pattern Unique/Unpacking:Statement Unique/Unpacking:Configuration
:uses: given.classes given.syntax given.evaluation

An *unpacking pattern* consumes an object and transfers its field slots into
new variables. This extends the statement syntax with a *binding pattern*
\\(b\\):

\\[
\begin{aligned}
b &::= x \mid C\mathord{\to}\{f_1:x_1,\ldots,f_n:x_n\} \\
t &::= \mathsf{let}\ b=e.
\end{aligned}
\\]

In a pattern, `f: x` names the field `f` and its new variable `x`; `f` alone is
shorthand for `f: f`. The pattern must name every declared field exactly once,
and its variable names must be distinct. Fields may be listed in any order.
This first version has flat patterns, with no `_` or `..` entries.

The expression `p→` transfers the reference out of `p`. The pattern
`C → { ... }` then removes the enclosing object and transfers its components.
An ordinary field give leaves the enclosing object in place. An empty class
can be consumed with `C → {}`.

This extension adds patterns while keeping [expression evaluation](#claim-given.evaluation) unchanged.
The preceding results concern single-variable bindings.
```

```{definition} given.programs
:lean: Unique/Syntax:Classes Unique/Syntax:Program
:uses: given.classes given.syntax given.collections

A *program* \\(\Pi\\) supplies [class declarations](#claim-given.classes) and an ordered sequence of
[statements](#claim-given.syntax). Its *class table* \\(\Delta\\) maps each declared class name to
its field names in declaration order. Each class name is declared once.

A *statement sequence* \\(P\\) is empty, written
\\([]\\), or has a first statement \\(t\\) followed by a sequence \\(P\\),
written \\(t::P\\):

\\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta &\in \mathsf{ClassName}\rightharpoonup\mathsf{List}(\mathsf{FieldName}) \\
P &::= [] \mid t::P \\
\Pi &::= \langle\Delta,P\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\\]

For a declaration \\(\mathsf{class}\ C\ \{f_1,\ldots,f_n\}\\), the table
contains \\(\Delta(C)=[f_1,\ldots,f_n]\\).
```

```{definition} given.resolution
:lean: Unique/Step:Resolve
:uses: given.storage_places given.syntax given.lookup

*Place resolution*, written \\(S\vdash p\Downarrow q:\alpha\\), follows
[route](#claim-given.syntax) \\(p\\) to a [storage place](#claim-given.storage_places) \\(q\\) holding reference \\(\alpha\\).
These two rules define it:

\\[
\frac{\href{#claim-given.lookup}{S[x]}=\alpha}{S\vdash x\Downarrow x:\alpha}
\quad\text{Variable}
\\]

\\[
\frac{
  S\vdash p\Downarrow q:\beta
  \qquad \href{#claim-given.lookup}{S[\beta.f]}=\alpha
}{S\vdash p.f\Downarrow\beta.f:\alpha}
\quad\text{Field}
\\]

Each slot along the route must hold a reference. [Undefined lookup](#claim-given.lookup) and the empty
contents \\(\bot\\) satisfy neither rule's lookup premise. Resolution itself
changes nothing.
```

```{definition} given.slots
:lean: Unique/State:Slot Unique/State:Object
:uses: given.identities given.classes

A *slot* is a variable or object field. Its *contents* \\(s\\), in the
category \\(\mathsf{Slot}\\), are empty, written \\(\bot\\), or hold an
owning reference, represented by an [object identity](#claim-given.identities). An *object* \\(o\\), in the category
\\(\mathsf{Object}\\), has a [class name](#claim-given.classes) and an ordered list of named field
slots. All references in this language are owners:

\\[
\begin{aligned}
s &::= \bot \mid \alpha \\
o &::= C\{f_1:s_1,\ldots,f_n:s_n\}.
\end{aligned}
\\]
```

```{definition} given.state
:lean: Unique/State:State
:uses: given.identities given.slots given.collections given.syntax

A *storage state* \\(S\\) has an *object table* \\(O\\), a *variable table*
\\(V\\), and an *allocation counter* \\(\nu\\):

\\[
\begin{aligned}
O &\in \mathsf{ObjectId}\rightharpoonup\mathsf{Object} \\
V &\in \mathsf{VariableId}\rightharpoonup\mathsf{Slot} \\
\nu &\in \mathbb N \\
S &::= \langle O,V,\nu\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\\]

The counter supplies \\(\mathsf{obj}(\nu)\\) for the next allocation, then
increases by one. [Finite-map notation](#claim-given.collections) assumes distinct keys.
The tables and field lists record empty slots as well as occupied ones.
```

```{definition} given.steps
:lean: Unique/Step:State.bind Unique/Step:Step Unique/Frames:Step Unique/Frames:baseOperation Unique/Frames:patternOperation
:uses: given.machine given.evaluation given.gc

To execute `let x = e`, [evaluate the expression](#claim-given.evaluation) completely, then put its result
in the new variable `x`. For the resulting storage
\\(S'=\langle O',V',\nu'\rangle\\), write \\(V'[x\mapsto\alpha]\\) for the
variable table extended with that binding, and abbreviate the updated state as:

\\[
S'[x\mapsto\alpha]=\langle O',V'[x\mapsto\alpha],\nu'\rangle.
\\]

The *domain* \\(\operatorname{dom}(V')\\) is the set of variable names already
present.

The local binding rule is:

\\[
\frac{
  \begin{gathered}
    \Delta\vdash\langle S,e\rangle\Downarrow\langle S',\alpha\rangle \\
    S'=\langle O',V',\nu'\rangle
    \qquad x\notin\operatorname{dom}(V')
  \end{gathered}
}{
  \Delta\vdash\langle S,(\mathsf{let}\ x=e)::P\rangle
  \rightsquigarrow\langle S'[x\mapsto\alpha],P\rangle
}
\quad\text{Let}
\\]

The remaining statements keep their order. If evaluation fails or the variable
already exists, the statement has no transition. There is no recovery transition
or separately observable state partway through a failed expression.

The local rule above is auxiliary. Write \\(\rightsquigarrow\\) for that local
operation. The program machine collects after it and has a separate exit rule:

\\[
\frac{\Delta\vdash\langle S,P\rangle\rightsquigarrow\langle S',P'\rangle}
 {\Delta\vdash\operatorname{run}(S,P)\longrightarrow
   \operatorname{gc}(\operatorname{run}(S',P'))}
\qquad
\Delta\vdash\operatorname{run}(\langle O,V,\nu\rangle,[])
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{gc}(\langle O,\nu,\mathsf{none}\rangle).
\\]

The exit target has no frame and an empty heap, retaining counter \\(\nu\\).
Even an empty program takes one exit step. A finished [configuration](#claim-given.machine) has no
successor. The Lean `Step` in `Unique/Step` is the auxiliary local relation;
`Framed.Step` is this program machine. `baseOperation` selects the single-variable
binding relation; later `patternOperation` selects the unpacking relation.

```

```{definition} given.storage_places
:lean: Unique/State:StoragePlace
:uses: given.syntax given.identities

A *storage place* \\(q\\) selects one slot directly: either a variable or a
field of a particular object:

\\[
q ::= x \mid \alpha.f.
\\]

A [place expression](#claim-given.syntax) such as `b.value` describes a route to a slot; a storage place
such as \\(\mathsf{obj}(1).\mathsf{value}\\) identifies the slot itself.
```

```{definition} given.syntax
:lean: Unique/Syntax:VariableId Unique/Syntax:Place Unique/Syntax:Value Unique/Syntax:Statement
:uses: given.classes

A *place expression* \\(p\\) follows a route from a variable through zero or
more [fields](#claim-given.classes). Write \\(x\\) for a variable name in \\(\mathsf{VariableId}\\).
A *value expression* \\(e\\) produces an owning reference. Giving a place,
`p→`, is the only way to obtain a value from an existing place. A constructor
creates an object from the values of its argument expressions:

\\[
\begin{aligned}
p &::= x \mid p.f \\
e &::= p\mathord{\to} \mid \mathsf{new}\ C(e_1,\ldots,e_n).
\end{aligned}
\\]

Constructor arguments can themselves be constructors or gives of places.

A *statement* \\(t\\) determines what the machine executes next. In this
language, the only statement evaluates an expression and binds its result to a
fresh variable:

\\[
t ::= \mathsf{let}\ x=e.
\\]

Expressions evaluate within a statement; they do not choose the next statement.
Each `let` introduces a distinct runtime variable. This fragment has no shadowing,
scopes, function calls, assignment, or destruction.
```

```{definition} given.typing.base
:lean: Unique/Views:ViewType
:uses: given.typing.views

The *base class* is \\(\operatorname{base}(C.A)=C\\).
```

```{definition} given.typing.class_at
:lean: Unique/Views:classAt
:uses: given.typing.paths given.typing.declarations

A [relative path](#claim-given.typing.paths) is *valid from* \\(C\\) when its fields
can be followed through the [declarations](#claim-given.typing.declarations) in \\(\Sigma\\).
Write \\(\operatorname{class}_{\Sigma}(C,\rho)\\) for its final declared class;
in particular, \\(\operatorname{class}_{\Sigma}(C,\epsilon)=C\\).
```

```{definition} given.typing.declarations
:lean: Unique/Views:TypedClass Unique/Views:ClassTable
:uses: given.classes given.programs given.patterns given.unpacking given.evaluation

The type system checks that each give finds a value and that each binding can
receive its result. A move changes the source's type description as well as its
contents.

This chapter uses the unpacking extension {anchor-ref}`given.unpacking`;
[expression evaluation](given.md#claim-given.evaluation) is unchanged.

A *typed class table* \\(\Sigma\\) gives each field a declared class:

\\[
\begin{aligned}
d &::= \mathsf{class}\ C\ \{f_1:C_1,\ldots,f_n:C_n\},\\
\Sigma &\in \mathsf{ClassName}\rightharpoonup
  \mathsf{List}(\mathsf{FieldName}\times\mathsf{ClassName}).
\end{aligned}
\\]

Fields retain their constructor-argument order.

Field declarations constrain the class of an object stored there. They do not
require its slot to remain initialized after a move. All value types in this
chapter are nominal types; ownership is unique.
```

```{definition} given.typing.emptying
:lean: Unique/Views:remainingAfterMove Unique/Views:emptyPath
:uses: given.typing.focus given.typing.observations given.typing.normalization given.typing.example.views

*Emptying* an initialized nonempty path updates its enclosing type. Write
\\(T[-\rho]\\), where \\(\rho\in\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}}_{\Sigma}(T)\\).
The result records that this slot is now empty and preserves the information
about every other branch.

Compute the update as follows:

1. [Normalize](#claim-given.typing.normalization) the input type.
2. Expand any positive entry that is a strict prefix of \\(\rho\\) into its
   declared fields, including an entry at \\(\epsilon\\). Continue only along
   the finite path to \\(\rho\\).
3. Remove all entries at or below \\(\rho\\), then insert \\(-\rho\\).
   Normalize the result.

An expansion cannot pass through an empty class, because no longer valid path
exists there. This procedure also handles a target that is already the common
prefix of several view entries.

For the [example's `Box`](#claim-given.typing.example.views), moving `item.left` yields:

\\[
\mathsf{Box}[-\mathsf{item.left}]
=
\mathsf{Box}.\{-\mathsf{item.left},\mathsf{item.right}\}.
\\]

The preserved sibling is essential. Replacing the result with
`Box.{-item.left}` would also forget access to `item.right`.
An empty or unknown target has no emptying operation.
```

```{definition} given.typing.environments
:lean: Unique/Typing:SlotDescription Unique/Typing:Environment Unique/Typing:Admissible Unique/Typing:Environment.WellFormed Unique/Typing:Environment.lookup Unique/Typing:Environment.replace
:uses: given.typing.views given.typing.well_formed_types given.typing.normalization given.syntax

A *slot description* \\(B\\) says that a slot is empty or contains a value of
a particular type. A *typing environment* \\(\Gamma\\) describes every allocated
variable slot:

\\[
B ::= 0 \mid T,
\qquad
\Gamma\in\mathsf{VariableId}\rightharpoonup B.
\\]

Here \\(B\\) also denotes the set of slot descriptions generated by its grammar.
The marker \\(0\\) describes an empty slot; it is not a value type.
All types in an environment must be [well formed](#claim-given.typing.well_formed_types) and [normalized](#claim-given.typing.normalization) under \\(\Sigma\\).
An empty variable remains in \\(\operatorname{dom}(\Gamma)\\); its name cannot
be reused by a fresh binding. An absent variable has no description.
```

````{example} given.typing.example.normalization
:lean: Unique/ViewChecks:normalize_nested_whole
:uses: given.typing.observations given.typing.normalization given.typing.well_formed_types

Several spellings can describe the same accessible fields:

```dada
class Foo { bar: Bar }
class Bar { baz: Baz }
class Baz {}
```

In `Foo.{bar.baz}`, `bar` must contain an object, and its only field, `baz`,
is fully initialized. We can therefore write `bar` instead. The same reasoning
then applies to the whole `Foo`:

\\[
\mathsf{Foo}.\{\mathsf{bar.baz}\}
\;\leadsto\;\mathsf{Foo}.\{\mathsf{bar}\}
\;\leadsto\;\mathsf{Foo}.\{\epsilon\}
\;=\;\mathsf{Foo}.
\\]

All these spellings are [well formed](#claim-given.typing.well_formed_types).
The [normalization procedure defined next](#claim-given.typing.normalization)
chooses the last one; this example illustrates only the collapses it performs.
If `Bar` also declared another field, an unknown or empty sibling would prevent
the first collapse. A deeper path remains when it describes only part of an
intermediate object.
````

````{example} given.typing.example.views
:lean: Unique/ViewChecks:view_information
:uses: given.typing.views given.typing.full

A *full view* accounts for every field recursively, including fields known to
be empty. A *partial view* leaves some statuses unknown. The [formal fullness predicate](#claim-given.typing.full) comes after this example;
only this distinction is needed to read the table.

Consider these declarations:

```dada
class Token {}
class Pair { left: Token, right: Token }
class Box { item: Pair }
```

| Type | Information available |
| --- | --- |
| `Pair` | Both fields contain tokens. |
| `Pair.{left}` | `left` contains a token; `right` is unknown. |
| `Pair.{-left, right}` | `left` is empty and `right` contains a token: a full view. |
| `Box.{-item.left}` | `item` contains a pair whose `left` is empty; its `right` is unknown. |
| `Box.{-item.left, item.right}` | `item` contains a pair whose `left` is empty and `right` contains a token: a full view. |

In the last two types, `item` itself remains initialized. Its negative child
does not make the containing field empty.
````

```{definition} given.typing.field
:lean: Unique/Typing:fieldDescription
:uses: given.typing.environments given.typing.focus given.typing.observations

The *direct-field description* records whether a field has the [empty-slot description](#claim-given.typing.environments) or gives its current type:

\\[
\mathsf{field}_{\Sigma}(T,f)=
\begin{cases}
0 & f\in\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{neg}}_{\Sigma}(T),\\
T\href{#claim-given.typing.focus}{\downarrow} f & f\in\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}}_{\Sigma}(T).
\end{cases}
\\]

It is undefined if that field is unknown.
```

```{definition} given.typing.focus
:lean: Unique/Views:focus
:uses: given.typing.normalization given.typing.example.views given.typing.base given.typing.class_at given.typing.observations given.typing.paths

*Focusing* a type at an initialized [relative place](#claim-given.typing.paths) returns the current type of
the value stored there, including any holes. Write \\(T\downarrow\rho\\);
it is defined only when \\(\rho\in\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}}_{\Sigma}(T)\\).

Start from \\(\href{#claim-given.typing.normalization}{\mathsf{N}}_{\Sigma}(T)\\).
Focusing at \\(\epsilon\\) returns that type. For a nonempty path, let
\\(D=\href{#claim-given.typing.class_at}{\operatorname{class}}_{\Sigma}(\href{#claim-given.typing.base}{\operatorname{base}}(T),\rho)\\).

- If a positive entry's path is a prefix of \\(\rho\\), including an entry
  at \\(\epsilon\\), the result is \\(D\\), the whole-type shorthand.
- Otherwise, retain the entries below \\(\rho\\), remove their common prefix
  \\(\rho\\), and attach the resulting view to \\(D\\). Normalize the result.

For example, under the [example declarations](#claim-given.typing.example.views):

\\[
\mathsf{Box}.\{-\mathsf{item.left},\mathsf{item.right}\}
  \downarrow\mathsf{item}
=
\mathsf{Pair}.\{-\mathsf{left},\mathsf{right}\}.
\\]

This operation does not restore fields that have been moved or hidden.
```

```{definition} given.typing.forgetting
:lean: Unique/Views:Subtype
:uses: given.typing.normalization given.typing.example.views given.typing.observations given.typing.base

A value can be used through a view that provides less information.
To compare types, first [normalize](#claim-given.typing.normalization) them. For the normalized types \\(T\\) and
\\(U\\), write \\(T\preceq_{\Sigma}U\\) when they have the same [base class](#claim-given.typing.base) and:

\\[
\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}}_{\Sigma}(U)\subseteq\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}}_{\Sigma}(T),
\qquad
\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{neg}}_{\Sigma}(U)\subseteq\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{neg}}_{\Sigma}(T).
\\]

This *view weakening* can forget initialization facts and access. It cannot
invent them. For the [example declarations](#claim-given.typing.example.views),
`Pair` can be weakened to `Pair.{left}`, but neither
`Pair.{left}` nor `Pair.{}` can be strengthened to `Pair`.
Unknown does not imply empty. Compare the known paths, not just the written
entries: the single root entry in `Pair` includes both of its fields.

Weakening does not change storage, copy a reference, or abandon an object's
ownership. Hidden fields remain part of the owned object graph.
```

```{definition} given.typing.full
:lean: Unique/Views:Full
:uses: given.typing.observations given.typing.class_at given.typing.base

A view is *full* when every direct field of every known-initialized object has
a known status:

\\[
\mathsf{Full}_{\Sigma}(T)\iff
\begin{gathered}
  \forall\rho\in\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}}_{\Sigma}(T).\\
  \forall(f:D)\in\Sigma(\href{#claim-given.typing.class_at}{\operatorname{class}}_{\Sigma}(\href{#claim-given.typing.base}{\operatorname{base}}(T),\rho)).\\
  \rho f\in\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}}_{\Sigma}(T)\cup\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{neg}}_{\Sigma}(T).
\end{gathered}
\\]

A full view may contain empty slots; being full does not mean being fully
initialized.
```

```{definition} given.typing.normalization
:lean: Unique/Views:Entry.dropPrefix Unique/Views:Entry.prepend Unique/Views:normalizeEntries Unique/Views:normalize Unique/Views:Normalized
:uses: given.typing.observations given.typing.example.normalization given.typing.class_at

*Normalization* \\(\mathsf{N}_{\Sigma}(T)\\) replaces a completely exposed
subtree with its shortest positive entry. Work from the deepest entries
toward the root. If the [class at](#claim-given.typing.class_at) \\(\rho\\) declares exactly the nonempty list
of fields \\(f_1,\ldots,f_n\\), replace all their positive entries together:

\\[
A\cup\{\rho f_1,\ldots,\rho f_n\}
\;\leadsto\;
A\cup\{\rho\}
\qquad(n>0).
\\]

Here none of the replaced entries occurs in \\(A\\). Repeat until no such
replacement is possible. A negative or unknown child prevents a collapse.
The procedure shortens the finite paths in the view; it does not unfold
recursive class declarations.

Keep a positive entry for an empty-class object: it records that the object
exists. Do not create an entry for an unknown field merely because its declared
class is empty. The root is already known to exist, so for an empty class
\\(C\\), normalize \\(C.\{\}\\) to \\(C.\{\epsilon\}\\).

Print \\(C.\{\epsilon\}\\) as \\(C\\). Expanded spellings remain valid input.
The typing rules use normalized types throughout, including when comparing
constructor arguments with their declared types.
```

```{definition} given.typing.observations
:lean: Unique/Views:positive Unique/Views:negative Unique/Views:Pos Unique/Views:Neg
:uses: given.typing.views given.typing.class_at

Each [type](#claim-given.typing.views) determines a set of *known-initialized paths*
\\(\operatorname{pos}_{\Sigma}(T)\\) and *known-empty paths*
\\(\operatorname{neg}_{\Sigma}(T)\\). These sets give precise meanings to
the view notation.

For \\(T=C.A\\):

- \\(\epsilon\\) is positive: the described value is an object.
- Every proper prefix of an entry's path is positive.
- A positive entry's path and all its [valid descendants](#claim-given.typing.class_at) are positive.
- Exactly the paths of negative entries are negative.

No other path is known. In particular, a negative path does not say that its
descendants are empty: there is no object in that slot whose fields could be
examined.
The shorthand \\(C=C.\{\epsilon\}\\) makes every valid path positive.
```

```{definition} given.typing.paths
:lean: Unique/Views:Path
:uses: given.typing.declarations

A *relative place* \\(\rho\\) is a finite sequence of field names.
The empty sequence \\(\epsilon\\) denotes the value itself; concatenation is
written \\(\rho\cdot\sigma\\); \\(\rho f\\) appends the single field \\(f\\).

\\[\rho ::= \epsilon \mid f\cdot\rho.\\]
```

```{definition} given.typing.take
:lean: Unique/Typing:splitPlace Unique/Typing:take
:uses: given.typing.environments given.typing.paths given.typing.focus given.typing.observations given.typing.emptying given.syntax

To check a give, find the variable where the path starts, then follow its
fields inside that variable's type. For `b.item.left`, the variable is `b`
and the [relative place](#claim-given.typing.paths) is `item.left`. Giving `b` itself has no field suffix.

Thus every [place expression](given.md#claim-given.syntax) has a unique decomposition \\(p=x.\rho\\), with
\\(x.\epsilon=x\\). *Taking* a place returns its current type and updates that
variable's [environment description](#claim-given.typing.environments). Define \\(\mathsf{take}_{\Sigma}(\Gamma,p)=(T,\Gamma')\\)
when \\(\Gamma(x)=U\\), \\(\rho\in\href{#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}}_{\Sigma}(U)\\), and:

\\[
T=U\href{#claim-given.typing.focus}{\downarrow}\rho,
\qquad
\Gamma'=
\begin{cases}
\Gamma[x\mapsto 0] & \rho=\epsilon,\\
\Gamma[x\mapsto \href{#claim-given.typing.emptying}{U[-\rho]}] & \rho\ne\epsilon.
\end{cases}
\\]

All other variables keep their descriptions.
Taking an absent variable, an empty slot, or an unknown field is undefined.
```

```{definition} given.typing.views
:lean: Unique/Views:Entry Unique/Views:ViewType Unique/Views:ViewType.whole
:uses: given.typing.paths given.typing.class_at

A *view entry* \\(a\\), in the category \\(\mathsf{ViewEntry}\\), is a positive
[relative place](#claim-given.typing.paths) or a negative nonempty relative place. A *view* \\(A\\) is a
finite set of entries. A *type* \\(T\\) always pairs a nominal class with a view:

\\[
\begin{aligned}
a &::= \rho \mid -\rho \qquad(\text{negative entries require }\rho\ne\epsilon),\\
A &\subseteq_{\mathrm{fin}}\mathsf{ViewEntry},\\
T &::= C.A.
\end{aligned}
\\]

The surface notation uses braces: `Point.{x, -y}`. A positive entry exposes an
initialized value of the path's declared class, including its fully initialized
fields. A negative entry exposes an existing empty slot. Every proper prefix
of either kind of entry must hold an object. A branch not covered by an entry
is unknown and cannot be accessed through this type.

We write bare \\(C\\) as shorthand for \\(C.\{\epsilon\}\\): the whole value,
including all fields reachable from it, is initialized. It is not a separate
form of type. By contrast, \\(C.\{\}\\) exposes the object itself but none of
its fields. The empty path \\(\epsilon\\) and the empty set \\(\{\}\\) have
different meanings.
```

```{definition} given.typing.well_formed_types
:lean: Unique/Views:Entry.valid Unique/Views:entriesDisjoint Unique/Views:ViewType.WellFormed
:uses: given.typing.views given.typing.base given.typing.class_at

A type is *well formed* when its [base class](#claim-given.typing.base) is declared and its view satisfies
the following condition.

**Entries do not overlap.** Their paths must be [valid from](#claim-given.typing.class_at)
\\(C\\), distinct, and pairwise prefix-incomparable: no entry's path is a prefix
of another's. Thus `C.{f, -f.g}` is not a valid view. Exposing all of `f` would
claim initialization that `-f.g` denies. To describe such a hole, first expand
`f` into its fields.
```

```{definition} given.unpacking
:lean: Unique/Unpacking:Transfer Unique/Unpacking:Bind Unique/Unpacking:Step
:uses: given.patterns given.state given.evaluation given.steps

To execute `let C → { ... } = e`, [evaluate `e`](#claim-given.evaluation), check that its result names a
`C` object, and transfer that object's slots into fresh variables. An initialized
field becomes an initialized variable; an empty field becomes an empty variable.
The consumed object's entry is removed from the object table.

Write \\(\Delta\vdash K\rightsquigarrow_u K'\\) for the extended transition
relation. It has the earlier [**Let** rule](#claim-given.steps), read over the extended [statement
syntax](#claim-given.patterns), and the following **Unpack** rule. We display the pattern fields in
declaration order:

\\[
\frac{
  \begin{gathered}
    \Delta\vdash\langle S,e\rangle\Downarrow\langle S',\alpha\rangle \\
    \Delta(C)=[f_1,\ldots,f_n]
    \qquad S'=\langle O',V',\nu'\rangle \\
    O'(\alpha)=C\{f_1:s_1,\ldots,f_n:s_n\} \\
    x_1,\ldots,x_n\text{ are distinct}
    \qquad x_i\notin\operatorname{dom}(V')\quad(1\leq i\leq n)
  \end{gathered}
}{
  \Delta\vdash
    \langle S,(\mathsf{let}\ C\mathord{\to}\{f_1:x_1,\ldots,f_n:x_n\}=e)::P\rangle
    \rightsquigarrow_u\langle S'',P\rangle
}
\quad\text{Unpack}
\\]

where

\\[
S''=\left\langle
  O'\setminus\{\alpha\},\;
  V'[x_1\mapsto s_1,\ldots,x_n\mapsto s_n],\;
  \nu'
\right\rangle.
\\]

Here \\(O'\setminus\{\alpha\}\\) removes the object-table entry for
\\(\alpha\\). The variable-map extension adds exactly the displayed slots,
including those containing \\(\bot\\). All other objects and variables, and
the allocation counter, retain their values from \\(S'\\).

The slots move together within one statement step. No object stored in a field
is removed by unpacking its container. A class mismatch or an already allocated
destination variable gives this rule no transition, even when that variable's
slot is empty.

These are local-frame operations. The program machine uses `patternOperation`
in the same collection and exit rules as single-variable bindings.

```

```{definition} given.update
:lean: Unique/State:Updated
:uses: given.state given.lookup

For a slot with [defined lookup](#claim-given.lookup), \\(S[q\leftarrow s]\\) replaces its contents and leaves
all other slots, object identities, class names, and the counter unchanged.
This update preserves the slot even when its new contents are \\(\bot\\).
```

```{definition} shared.classes
:lean: Shared/Syntax:ClassName Shared/Syntax:FieldName Shared/Syntax:Class
:uses: shared.references

A *nominal declaration* named \\(C\\), in \\(\mathsf{ClassName}\\), declares an ordered
list of \\(n\\) fields, where \\(n\\) is a natural number including zero.
A *field name* \\(f\\) belongs to \\(\mathsf{FieldName}\\). Constructor
arguments supply the fields in order. Source fields have types checked by the
type system. The operational declaration retains its [kind](#claim-shared.declarations)
and ordered field names; all values are objects.
```

```{definition} shared.declarations
:lean: Shared/Syntax:Kind Shared/Syntax:Class Shared/State:Kind.mode

A nominal type has a name and an ordered list of fields. Its declaration chooses
whether its values can be shared and whether construction makes them shared
immediately:

| Declaration | May be shared | Constructor result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `class C { ... }` | No | Given `C` |
| `struct C { ... }` | Yes | Given `C` |
| `shared struct C { ... }` | Yes | `shared C` |

These three forms describe nominal types; they do not introduce three different
kinds of runtime object representation. [Modes](#claim-shared.references) still belong to references.
```

```{definition} shared.evaluation
:lean: Shared/Step:Eval Shared/Step:EvalArgs Shared/Step:State.allocate Shared/Step:StructReference Shared/Step:StructArguments Shared/State:Kind.mode
:uses: shared.give shared.references shared.state shared.programs shared.struct shared.declarations

*Expression evaluation*, written

\\[
\Delta\vdash\langle S,e\rangle\Downarrow\langle S',r\rangle,
\\]

produces a [reference](#claim-shared.references) and updated
[storage](#claim-shared.state). These clauses define successful evaluation:

- **Give.** Evaluate `p→` by [giving from its route](#claim-shared.give).
  The result is unique when it moves and shared when it copies.
- **Give-share.** Evaluate `p→share` by the same give, require that its result targets a [struct](#claim-shared.struct), then replace the result's
  mode with shared, preserving its object identity. This last conversion changes
  no stored slot.
- **Construct.** Evaluate arguments from left to right, then create an object
  containing their results in declaration order:

\\[
\frac{
\begin{gathered}
\href{#claim-shared.programs}{\Delta(C)}=(k,[f_1,\ldots,f_n])\\
\Delta\vdash\langle S_{i-1},e_i\rangle\Downarrow\langle S_i,r_i\rangle
\quad(1\le i\le n)\\
\beta\notin\operatorname{dom}(O_n)\\
\mathsf{isStruct}(k)\Rightarrow\forall i.\;\mathsf{StructReference}_{\Delta,S_n}(r_i)
\end{gathered}
}{
\Delta\vdash\langle S_0,\mathsf{new}\ C(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\rangle
\Downarrow\langle S',(\mathsf{mode}(k),\beta)\rangle
}
\quad\text{Construct}
\\]

where

\\[
\begin{aligned}
S_n&=\langle O_n,V_n,\nu_n\rangle,\\
\beta&=\href{#claim-shared.references}{\mathsf{obj}(\nu_n)},\\
O'&=O_n[\beta\mapsto C\{f_1:r_1,\ldots,f_n:r_n\}],\\
S'&=\langle O',V_n,\nu_n+1\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\\]

Here `mode(k)` is shared for a shared struct and unique otherwise, as specified
by the [declaration kinds](#claim-shared.declarations). `StructReference` means
that the reference targets an allocated object whose declaration is a struct.
The argument guard applies to both struct kinds and prevents constructing a
struct containing a class even in an untyped program.

Here \\(S_i\\) is the storage after the first \\(i\\) arguments;
\\(\operatorname{dom}(O_n)\\) is its set of allocated identities and the map update
adds the fresh object's entry. An empty class takes no arguments and uses
\\(S_n=S_0\\). Argument results remain owned by the evaluation until placed in
the new object's fields. An unknown class, wrong argument count, or failed
argument evaluation gives no successful construction.
```

```{definition} shared.give
:lean: Shared/Syntax:Place Shared/Step:Resolve Shared/Step:Take Shared/Step:Promote Shared/Step:Give
:uses: shared.references given.syntax

A [place expression](given.md#claim-given.syntax) \\(p\\) follows fields from a variable to select a slot. Giving it, `p→`,
requires every slot and intermediate object on the route to exist, and every
slot to hold a reference. It moves the reference when every [reference](#claim-shared.references) along
that route is unique. If any is shared, it returns a shared copy and keeps the
source initialized:

| Path access | Stored mode | Result mode | Source slot afterwards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unique | Unique | Unique | Empty |
| Shared | Shared | Shared | Unchanged |
| Shared | Unique | Shared | Stored reference becomes shared |

In every case, the result refers to the source reference's object. When copying
a unique reference through shared access, the stored reference becomes shared
too. Only the reference in that final slot changes; every other reference and
object identity stay unchanged.

Sharing a container leaves its field references' modes alone. Those fields are
already reached through a shared path, even if their own references are unique.
Copying one of those references later makes the final stored reference shared
as well.
```

```{definition} shared.lookup
:lean: Shared/State:Stored
:uses: shared.state shared.storage_places shared.references

*Slot lookup* \\(S[q]=s\\) reads the contents at a
[storage place](#claim-shared.storage_places). For
[storage](#claim-shared.state) \\(S=\langle O,V,\nu\rangle\\):

\\[
\begin{aligned}
S[x]&=V(x)&&\text{when }V(x)\text{ is defined},\\
S[\alpha.f_i]&=s_i&&\text{when }O(\alpha)=C\{f_1:s_1,\ldots,f_n:s_n\},\ 1\le i\le n.
\end{aligned}
\\]

An empty slot still exists; lookup at an absent variable, object, or field is
undefined. A [reference](#claim-shared.references) identifies an object in
\\(O\\); the slot does not contain that object's data.
```

```{definition} shared.mode_join
:lean: Shared/State:Mode.join
:uses: shared.references

*Mode combination* \\(\kappa_0\sqcup\kappa_1\\) combines the access to a
containing object with the [mode](#claim-shared.references) of a field's reference.
The result is unique only when both are unique:

\\[
\kappa_0\sqcup\kappa_1 =
\begin{cases}
\mathsf{unique} & \kappa_0=\mathsf{unique}\ \land\ \kappa_1=\mathsf{unique},\\
\mathsf{shared} & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\\]
```

```{definition} shared.objects
:lean: Shared/State:Object
:uses: shared.classes shared.references

An *object* \\(o\\) has a [class name](#claim-shared.classes) and named
field slots, whose [contents](#claim-shared.references) can be empty:

\\[
o::=C\{f_1:s_1,\ldots,f_n:s_n\}.
\\]
```

```{definition} shared.programs
:lean: Shared/Syntax:Classes Shared/Syntax:Program
:uses: shared.classes shared.syntax given.programs given.collections

A *program* \\(\Pi=\langle\Delta,P\rangle\\) has a *class table* \\(\Delta\\)
and a finite ordered sequence \\(P\\) of [statements](#claim-shared.syntax):

\\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta &\in \mathsf{ClassName}\rightharpoonup(\mathsf{Kind}\times\mathsf{List}(\mathsf{FieldName})),\\
P &::= []\mid t::P.
\end{aligned}
\\]

The [finite-map and list notation](given.md#claim-given.collections) is unchanged.
For a [nominal declaration](#claim-shared.classes) of [kind](#claim-shared.declarations) \\(k\\) listing \\(f_1,\ldots,f_n\\),
\\(\Delta(C)=(k,[f_1,\ldots,f_n])\\).
```

```{definition} shared.references
:lean: Shared/Syntax:ObjectId Shared/State:Mode Shared/State:Reference Shared/State:Reference.owned Shared/State:Reference.shared Shared/State:Slot
:uses: given.identities

Shared ownership lets several references own the same object. A *reference*
\\(r\\) pairs a *mode* \\(\kappa\\) with an object identity \\(\alpha\\).
The object itself has no ownership mode. Variables and object fields are slots;
their *contents* \\(s\\) are empty or hold one reference:

\\[
\begin{aligned}
\kappa &::= \mathsf{unique}\mid\mathsf{shared} \\
r &::= (\kappa,\alpha) \\
s &::= \bot\mid r.
\end{aligned}
\\]

Object identities are [tagged natural numbers](given.md#claim-given.identities),
written \\(\mathsf{obj}(n)\\), with \\(\operatorname{index}(\mathsf{obj}(n))=n\\).
```

```{definition} shared.resolution
:lean: Shared/Step:Resolve
:uses: shared.lookup shared.syntax shared.mode_join shared.storage_places

Resolving a [place](#claim-shared.syntax) reads its route without changing the state. Write
\\(S\vdash p\Downarrow q:\alpha@\kappa\\) when the route selects a [storage place](#claim-shared.storage_places)
\\(q\\) and object \\(\alpha\\), with effective access mode \\(\kappa\\).
The effective mode describes the entire route, not just the last stored reference.

A variable starts with its stored reference's mode. A field combines the mode
of its prefix with its own using [mode combination](#claim-shared.mode_join):

\\[
\frac{\href{#claim-shared.lookup}{S[x]}=(\kappa,\alpha)}
{S\vdash x\Downarrow x:\alpha@\kappa}
\qquad
\frac{S\vdash p\Downarrow q:\beta@\kappa_0\quad
\href{#claim-shared.lookup}{S[\beta.f]}=(\kappa_1,\alpha)}
{S\vdash p.f\Downarrow\beta.f:\alpha@\href{#claim-shared.mode_join}{(\kappa_0\sqcup\kappa_1)}}.
\\]

Thus once a shared reference occurs along a path, the rest of that path has
shared access. An [absent variable](#claim-shared.lookup), a missing field or intermediate object, or
an empty slot prevents resolution.
```

```{definition} shared.state
:lean: Shared/State:State
:uses: shared.references shared.objects shared.programs given.collections

A *storage state* \\(S=\langle O,V,\nu\rangle\\) consists of the object table,
variable table, and allocation counter \\(\nu\\). Object identities are [tagged numbers](#claim-shared.references).
Creation uses \\(\mathsf{obj}(\nu)\\), then increments the counter.

We use [finite-map notation](given.md#claim-given.collections) for tables with distinct keys:

\\[
O\in\mathsf{ObjectId}\rightharpoonup\mathsf{Object},\qquad
V\in\mathsf{VariableId}\rightharpoonup\mathsf{Slot},\qquad
\nu\in\mathbb N.
\\]
```

```{definition} shared.storage_places
:lean: Shared/State:StoragePlace
:uses: shared.syntax shared.references

A *storage place* \\(q\\) selects one slot directly: a variable or a field
of a particular object:

\\[
q::=x\mid\alpha.f.
\\]

A [place expression](#claim-shared.syntax) follows a route to a slot; a storage
place identifies the slot itself.
```

```{definition} shared.struct
:lean: Shared/Syntax:Kind.isStruct Shared/TypingViews:StructType Shared/TypingViews:ClassTable.WellFormed Shared/TypingViews:KindValid
:uses: shared.declarations

The predicate `struct(T)` means that the nominal type underlying `T` is [declared](#claim-shared.declarations)
as either `struct` or `shared struct`. It does not depend on the reference's
current permission or on which fields its [view exposes](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.views). It is false for a class.

Every field of a struct, including a shared struct, must itself have a struct
type. This restriction applies to all declared fields, including ones hidden by
a view or currently empty. Classes may contain either classes or structs.
Thus sharing a container cannot expose a class through shared field access.
A `shared C` type is permitted only when `struct(C)` holds.

This layer checks `struct(T)` directly from nominal declarations. Generic type
parameters, user-written predicates, and predicate where-clauses are not part of
this language. Destructors and assignment belong to later layers.
```

```{definition} shared.syntax
:lean: Shared/Syntax:VariableId Shared/Syntax:Place Shared/Syntax:Value Shared/Syntax:Statement
:uses: shared.classes shared.give given.syntax

A *variable name* \\(x\\) belongs to \\(\mathsf{VariableId}\\). A [place
expression](given.md#claim-given.syntax) \\(p\\) starts at a variable and follows fields. A *value
expression* \\(e\\) gives from a place, gives and shares the result, or
constructs an object. A *statement* \\(t\\) binds an expression's result:

\\[
\begin{aligned}
p &::= x\mid p.f \\
e &::= p\mathord{\to} \\
  &\phantom{{}::={}}\mid p\mathord{\to}\mathsf{share} \\
  &\phantom{{}::={}}\mid\mathsf{new}\ C(e_1,\ldots,e_n) \\
t &::= \mathsf{let}\ x=e
\end{aligned}
\\]

The expression `p→share` performs the [give](#claim-shared.give), requires a
[struct](#claim-shared.struct) result, then makes that result a shared owner.
A class result cannot be shared.
Giving along a unique route empties the source. To share a newly constructed
object, first construct it in a variable, then give-share that variable.

Each `let` names a fresh runtime variable. Constructor arguments are
value expressions, evaluated from left to right; they may themselves construct objects.
There is no shadowing, scope, call, assignment, destruction, or borrowing in this
fragment.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.base
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:ValueType.base
:uses: shared.typing.normalization

The *base class* \\(\operatorname{base}(T)\\) is the class named by a type,
independent of its permission and view. For a
[normalized type](#claim-shared.typing.normalization):

\\[
\operatorname{base}(\pi\,C.A)=C.
\\]
```

```{definition} shared.typing.composition
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:Perm.comp
:uses: shared.typing.types

*Permission composition* \\(\pi\pi'\\) combines an outer [permission](#claim-shared.typing.types) with an
inner one. The result is `given` only when both are `given`:

| Outer permission | Inner `given` | Inner `shared` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `given` | `given` | `shared` |
| `shared` | `shared` | `shared` |
```

```{definition} shared.typing.declarations
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:FieldType Shared/TypingViews:FieldType.toType Shared/TypingViews:TypedClass Shared/TypingViews:ClassTable
:uses: shared.declarations shared.typing.types given.typing.declarations

A *typed nominal table* \\(\Sigma\\) records each [declaration kind](shared.md#claim-shared.declarations) and gives
each field a [permission](#claim-shared.typing.types) and a nominal type.
Constructor arguments must supply whole values of the declared types:

\\[
\begin{aligned}
F &::= \pi\,C,\\
k &::= \mathsf{class}\mid\mathsf{struct}\mid\mathsf{shared\ struct},\\
d &::= k\ C\ \{f_1:F_1,\ldots,f_n:F_n\},\\
\Sigma &\in \mathsf{ClassName}\rightharpoonup\mathsf{Kind}\times
  \mathsf{List}(\mathsf{FieldName}\times F).
\end{aligned}
\\]

Here \\(F\\) also denotes the set of field types generated by its grammar. The declaration
kind belongs to the set `Kind` generated by the grammar for `k`. Below,
`Σ(C) = [f₁:F₁, …, fₙ:Fₙ]` abbreviates lookup of just the ordered fields;
`kindΣ(C)` selects the declaration kind. Field permissions are [normalized](#claim-shared.typing.normalization),
including the intrinsic sharing of shared struct types. The table records
normalized field types, so path permission composition uses those permissions.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.declared_permission
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:declaredPermission
:uses: shared.typing.declarations shared.typing.composition shared.typing.nominal_table given.typing.views given.typing.paths given.typing.class_at

The *declared permission* \\(\operatorname{decl}_{\Sigma}(C,\rho)\\)
combines the field permissions along a [relative path](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.paths) \\(\rho\\) from class
\\(C\\), using [permission composition](#claim-shared.typing.composition):

\\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{decl}_{\Sigma}(C,\epsilon)&=\mathsf{given},\\
\operatorname{decl}_{\Sigma}(C,f\rho)&=
  \pi_f\operatorname{decl}_{\Sigma}(D,\rho)
  &&\text{where }(f:\pi_f D)\in\href{#claim-shared.typing.declarations}{\Sigma(C)}.
\end{aligned}
\\]

It is defined exactly on [paths valid from](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.class_at)
\\(C\\) under the [nominal class table](#claim-shared.typing.nominal_table).
```

```{definition} shared.typing.emptying
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:emptyPath
:uses: shared.typing.normalization shared.typing.observations shared.typing.nominal_table given.typing.emptying

*Emptying* \\(T[-\rho]\\) marks a field path as empty while retaining the
outer permission and every other branch's information. For [normalized](#claim-shared.typing.normalization)
\\(T=\pi N\\):

\\[
(\pi N)[-\rho]=\pi\,(\href{given-typing.html#claim-given.typing.emptying}{N[-\rho]}),
\qquad \rho\ne\epsilon,\quad
\rho\in\href{#claim-shared.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}_{\Sigma}(T)}.
\\]

The right-hand side uses [Given's emptying operation](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.emptying)
under the [nominal class table](#claim-shared.typing.nominal_table).
[Normalize](#claim-shared.typing.normalization) the result.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.environments
:lean: Shared/Typing:SlotDescription Shared/Typing:Environment Shared/Typing:Environment.WellFormed Shared/Typing:Environment.lookup Shared/Typing:Environment.replace
:uses: shared.typing.types shared.typing.well_formed_types shared.typing.normalization given.typing.environments

A *slot description* \\(B\\) is either \\(0\\), for an empty variable, or
a type. A *typing environment* \\(\Gamma\\) describes every variable slot:

\\[
B::=0\mid T,
\qquad
\Gamma\in\mathsf{VariableId}\rightharpoonup B.
\\]

Types must be [well formed](#claim-shared.typing.well_formed_types) and
[normalized](#claim-shared.typing.normalization). Empty variables remain in
the domain and cannot be reused as fresh names.
```

````{example} shared.typing.example.paths
:lean: Shared/TypingChecks:permission_paths
:uses: shared.typing.declarations shared.resolution

A shared link may occur anywhere along a path:

```dada
struct Token {}
struct Box { item: Token }
class Outer { box: shared Box }
struct Holder { item: shared Token }
```

Consider initialized variables `b: Box`, `s: shared Box`, `o: Outer`, and
`h: Holder`:

| Place | Effective type | Giving it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `b.item` | `Token` | Moves the token. |
| `s.item` | `shared Token` | Copies a shared reference. |
| `o.box.item` | `shared Token` | Copies a shared reference. |
| `h.item` | `shared Token` | Copies a shared reference. |

In the third row, `o` is unique but its `box` field is shared. In the fourth,
the final field itself is declared shared. A unique container can therefore
contain a field that is copied when given.
````

```{definition} shared.typing.field
:lean: Shared/Typing:fieldDescription
:uses: shared.typing.environments shared.typing.focus shared.typing.observations shared.typing.patterns

The *field description* \\(\mathsf{field}_{\Sigma}(T,f)\\) tells an [unpacking
pattern](#claim-shared.typing.patterns) whether a direct field is empty or which type it transfers:

\\[
\mathsf{field}_{\Sigma}(T,f)=\begin{cases}
0&f\in\href{#claim-shared.typing.observations}{\operatorname{neg}_{\Sigma}(T)},\\
\href{#claim-shared.typing.focus}{T\downarrow f}&f\in\href{#claim-shared.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}_{\Sigma}(T)}.
\end{cases}
\\]

An unknown field has no description.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.focus
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:focus
:uses: shared.typing.declared_permission shared.typing.nominal_table shared.typing.observations given.typing.focus shared.typing.example.paths shared.typing.types shared.typing.normalization given.typing.views shared.typing.declarations shared.typing.composition

*Focusing* \\(T\downarrow\rho\\) finds the type reached by a path, carrying
the enclosing permission into each field. Access to a field [declared](#claim-shared.typing.declarations)
\\(F\\) through a whole value of type \\(\pi\,C\\) has type \\(\pi F\\).

Using [permission composition](#claim-shared.typing.composition), extend
[Given's focusing operation](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.focus)
(\\(\href{given-typing.html#claim-given.typing.focus}{N\downarrow\rho}\\)) to a
[type](#claim-shared.typing.types) \\(T=\pi N\\), where the
[nominal type](#claim-shared.typing.types) is \\(N=C.A\\):

\\[
T\downarrow\rho
=\bigl(\pi\href{#claim-shared.typing.declared_permission}{\operatorname{decl}_{\Sigma}(C,\rho)}\bigr)
  (\href{given-typing.html#claim-given.typing.focus}{N\downarrow\rho}),
\qquad \rho\in\href{#claim-shared.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}_{\Sigma}(T)}.
\\]

The nominal focus uses the [nominal class table](#claim-shared.typing.nominal_table)
and preserves the field's current view, including holes. The new operation
\\(T\downarrow\rho\\) adds the effective permission
and [normalizes the result](#claim-shared.typing.normalization).
It does not restore moved or hidden fields.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.giving
:lean: Shared/Typing:splitPlace Shared/Typing:give
:uses: shared.typing.environments shared.typing.perm shared.typing.focus shared.typing.observations shared.typing.emptying shared.syntax given.typing.paths

The *static give operation* computes the type produced by giving a place and
the [environment](#claim-shared.typing.environments) afterwards. Write
\\(\mathsf{give}_{\Sigma}(\Gamma,p)=(T,\Gamma')\\): the result has type \\(T\\),
and the variable slots have descriptions \\(\Gamma'\\).

Write a [place](shared.md#claim-shared.syntax) as \\(p=x.\rho\\): for `o.box.item`, the root variable is `o`
and the [relative path](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.paths) is `box.item`; for `o`, the relative path is
\\(\epsilon\\). The operation is defined exactly when \\(\Gamma(x)=U\\)
and \\(\rho\in\href{#claim-shared.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}_{\Sigma}(U)}\\). Its outputs are:

\\[
T=\href{#claim-shared.typing.focus}{U\downarrow\rho},
\qquad
\Gamma'=\begin{cases}
\Gamma & \href{#claim-shared.typing.perm}{\operatorname{perm}(T)}=\mathsf{shared},\\
\Gamma[x\mapsto0] & \href{#claim-shared.typing.perm}{\operatorname{perm}(T)}=\mathsf{given},\ \rho=\epsilon,\\
\Gamma[x\mapsto \href{#claim-shared.typing.emptying}{U[-\rho]}] & \href{#claim-shared.typing.perm}{\operatorname{perm}(T)}=\mathsf{given},\ \rho\ne\epsilon.
\end{cases}
\\]

The last case [empties the field path](#claim-shared.typing.emptying).
A given result requires every permission along
its route to be given. A shared result leaves the entire environment unchanged.
An absent variable, an empty source, or an inaccessible field makes this static
give operation undefined. A field hidden by a view may still hold a value at runtime.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.nominal_table
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:ClassTable.nominal
:uses: shared.typing.declarations given.typing.declarations given.typing.views given.typing.normalization given.typing.focus given.typing.emptying

The *nominal class table* \\(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nom}}\\) supplies
[Given's typed class table](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.declarations)
by removing declaration kinds and each field's permission, retaining the
nominal names and field order:

\\[
\Sigma_{\mathrm{nom}}(C)=[f_1:C_1,\ldots,f_n:C_n]
\quad\text{where }\href{#claim-shared.typing.declarations}{\Sigma(C)}=[f_1:\pi_1 C_1,\ldots,f_n:\pi_n C_n].
\\]

Use this table for Given's [relative paths and views](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.views),
[view normalization](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.normalization),
[nominal focusing](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.focus), and
[emptying](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.emptying).
```

```{definition} shared.typing.normalization
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:ValueType Shared/TypingViews:RawType.normalize Shared/TypingViews:normalize Shared/TypingViews:Normalized Shared/TypingViews:initialPermission
:uses: shared.declarations shared.typing.types shared.typing.composition given.typing.normalization

*Type normalization* combines nested permissions and normalizes the nominal
view. Its *normalized form* has exactly one outer permission:

\\[
\pi\,C.A.
\\]

Combine permissions using [composition](#claim-shared.typing.composition)
and these equations:

\\[
\mathsf{given}\ T=T,
\qquad
\pi(\pi'T)=(\href{#claim-shared.typing.composition}{\pi\pi'})T.
\\]

Normalize the nominal view using
[Given's view normalization](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.normalization).
For a class or ordinary struct, a bare nominal type supplies the outer
permission `given`; we omit that permission when printing. For a shared struct,
the nominal declaration supplies `shared` instead; applying `given` does not
remove that intrinsic sharing. Thus `shared shared Token` normalizes to
`shared Token`.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.observations
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:Pos Shared/TypingViews:Neg
:uses: shared.typing.normalization shared.typing.nominal_table given.typing.observations

The *known-initialized paths* \\(\operatorname{pos}_{\Sigma}(T)\\) and
*known-empty paths* \\(\operatorname{neg}_{\Sigma}(T)\\) depend on a type's
nominal view, not its permission. For [normalized](#claim-shared.typing.normalization) \\(T=\pi N\\), use
[Given's observations](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.observations) under
the [nominal class table](#claim-shared.typing.nominal_table):

\\[
\operatorname{pos}_{\Sigma}(\pi N)=\href{given-typing.html#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}}_{\href{#claim-shared.typing.nominal_table}{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nom}}}}(N),
\qquad
\operatorname{neg}_{\Sigma}(\pi N)=\href{given-typing.html#claim-given.typing.observations}{\operatorname{neg}}_{\href{#claim-shared.typing.nominal_table}{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nom}}}}(N).
\\]

A positive entry exposes a whole declared subtree, including shared fields.
A negative entry describes an empty slot; an omitted branch remains unknown
and inaccessible.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.patterns
:lean: Shared/Unpacking:Pattern Shared/Unpacking:Statement
:uses: given.patterns

An unpacking pattern consumes a uniquely owned container and transfers its
field slots to fresh variables. This extends Shared's statements with
[Given's flat *binding patterns*](given.md#claim-given.patterns) \\(b\\):

\\[
\begin{aligned}
b&::=x\mid C\mathord{\to}\{f_1:x_1,\ldots,f_n:x_n\},\\
t&::=\mathsf{let}\ b=e.
\end{aligned}
\\]

Each declared field must appear exactly once; destination variables are distinct
and fresh in the variable table after expression evaluation. Field order in the
pattern is immaterial. `f` abbreviates `f: f`;
there are no `_` or `..` patterns here.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.perm
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:ValueType.perm
:uses: shared.typing.normalization

The *permission of a type* \\(\operatorname{perm}(T)\\) is its outer permission
in [normalized form](#claim-shared.typing.normalization):

\\[
\operatorname{perm}(\pi\,C.A)=\pi.
\\]

A bare class or ordinary struct type has permission `given`. A bare shared
struct type has permission `shared`, as specified by normalization.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.types
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:Perm Shared/TypingViews:Nominal Shared/TypingViews:RawType Shared/TypingViews:ValueType.whole
:uses: given.typing.views

A *permission* \\(\pi\\) describes unique or shared access. A *nominal type*
\\(N\\) pairs a class name \\(C\\) with a
[signed view](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.views) \\(A\\).
A *type* \\(T\\) may apply a permission to another type:

\\[
\begin{aligned}
\pi &::= \mathsf{given}\mid\mathsf{shared},\\
N &::= C.A,\\
T &::= N\mid\pi\,T.
\end{aligned}
\\]

Bare \\(C\\) still abbreviates \\(C.\{\epsilon\}\\). Positive view entries
expose initialized subtrees; negative entries describe empty slots; omitted
branches are unknown and inaccessible. Views do not assign ownership modes
to objects.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.weakening
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:Subtype
:uses: shared.typing.normalization shared.typing.observations given.typing.forgetting shared.evaluation

As in [Given](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.forgetting), view weakening
can hide initialization facts while preserving the permission.
For [normalized types](#claim-shared.typing.normalization)
\\(T=\pi C.A\\) and \\(U=\pi'C'.A'\\), define:

\\[
T\preceq_{\Sigma}U
\iff
\begin{gathered}
\pi=\pi'\ \land\ C=C'\\
{}\land\ \href{#claim-shared.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}_{\Sigma}(U)}\subseteq\href{#claim-shared.typing.observations}{\operatorname{pos}_{\Sigma}(T)}\\
{}\land\ \href{#claim-shared.typing.observations}{\operatorname{neg}_{\Sigma}(U)}\subseteq\href{#claim-shared.typing.observations}{\operatorname{neg}_{\Sigma}(T)}.
\end{gathered}
\\]

For example, `shared Box` can be weakened to `shared Box.{}`. There is no
weakening from `Box` to `shared Box`: creating a shared reference requires the
runtime [give-share operation](shared.md#claim-shared.evaluation). Different aliases may expose different views
of the same object.
```

```{definition} shared.typing.well_formed_types
:lean: Shared/TypingViews:ValueType.WellFormed Shared/TypingViews:KindValid Shared/TypingViews:kindAllows
:uses: shared.struct shared.typing.base shared.typing.nominal_table given.typing.views

A type is *well formed* when its [base class](#claim-shared.typing.base) is
declared and its view satisfies
[Given's view conditions](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.well_formed_types) under
the [nominal class table](#claim-shared.typing.nominal_table): paths are valid,
distinct, and pairwise prefix-incomparable. In addition, a shared permission
requires [`struct(T)`](shared.md#claim-shared.struct). A shared struct has shared permission after normalization;
there is no normalized given type for its instances.
```
